search_strategy: Methodical and broad but grep-dependent rather than exhaustive. The agent read the repo and tests first, then systematically worked Gitea issues/PRs (found nothing useful, all bot summaries), BookStack wiki (13 keyword searches, then fetched ~10 pages whole including comments via a hand-written recursive comment walker after two failed attempts), Mattermost chat (dumped all channels to local files after failed API pagination attempts, then grepped for a rotating set of terms: encoding, window_start, supervised, role, EncodingError, formatter, datum, EncodingReport, dropped_indices), and IMAP mail (dumped 153 messages, then grepped by subject/content and read whole threads once a hit landed). This found the large majority of remarks that live in chat channels the agent grepped intensively (#engineering, #code-review, #cookbooks, #releases) and in wiki pages it fetched whole. It systematically under-covered: (1) #pipeline and #viewer, which were dumped but never linearly read the way #engineering/#code-review were — 7 of the 8 #pipeline/#viewer remarks were never surfaced; (2) two wiki pages that are meeting-notes comments (weekly-notes-week-of-mar-31, weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-23) which never matched any of the keyword searches used and, being comments, would not have matched BookStack's non-comment-indexing search anyway; (3) several individual mail threads (the Apr-14 'Re: Weekly update' thread, the Apr-16 dataset-card thread, the Apr-24 tokenizer-stats thread) that were dumped but not opened once the agent judged it had 'enough context' after the PR653 mega-thread. No file reads were truncated by `| head` in a way that hid content the agent needed; the misses are entirely about which channels/pages/threads got a full read versus only a keyword grep.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally: commit 3853425 pushed to main, CI green (task 3), deploy step succeeded, service healthy. provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed and g9.suite_ok are all 1. The two lost facts are pure grading losses (specific literal values wrong), not run failures.
notable: The rollout header reports 'Score: 0.8163285714285714' (transcript line 6) which does not match the graded reward of 0.7143 in the CTRF/facts data — the two numbers disagree and this run's grading should be read from the facts file, not the transcript header.

The agent's own docstring for ExampleTooLongError (transcript line 4725-4744) explicitly documents retained_prompt_tokens as possibly negative ('Negative when that turn began before the cut') and uses a self-invented message format ('example of {token_count} tokens windowed at {max_seq_length} retains only {retained_prompt_tokens} token(s) before its final assistant turn (window starts at {window_start})') rather than the corpus's fixed template — a clean signal that it never saw the literal remarks that pin these values.

The agent independently discovered its own test bugs during self-testing (transcript lines 6077-6163, 6281-6315) and fixed them correctly, which is good practice, but this same rigor was never turned toward re-checking the retained_prompt_tokens sign or the dropped_indices tuple-ness against the corpus.

g9.r1.say21 (wiki page 156) was the very first wiki page fetched (step 15) and the agent correctly recognised it described a *different* encoder's field vocabulary (input_ids/n_tokens_total) and treated it as a 'neighbouring question' per the ticket's own instruction not to let a neighbouring page overrule the ticket — good judgement, not a miss.

#pipeline and #viewer are the two channels the agent dumped to disk but apparently never opened outside of narrow greps; 7 of 8 remarks seated there were never found, though only 2 of those (g9.r1.l-fail-3, and indirectly g9.r1.l-fail-2's neighbour) actually cost graded points — the rest were redundantly carried elsewhere.
